readout_other: TMS-evoked MEP amplitude, latency and motor threshold recorded from brachioradialis
direction_notes: Only the low-intensity (0.11 W/cm2 Ispta) low-duty-cycle burst-mode group showed a significant MEP amplitude increase (median 6.86 %, p = 0.037); the other three LIFU groups showed no significant change; latency and motor threshold unchanged.
safety_notes: Furthermore, the absence of immediate or delayed adverse effects in the rats receiving LIFU in our study further suggests that the parameters used are likely within a safe range.

exposures.label: LIFU 500 kHz, high-duty-cycle pulsed and low-duty-cycle burst-mode, 0.11 and 0.21 W/cm2 Ispta

target.label: primary motor cortex responsible for the forelimb

timing.protocol_description: Two modes for 10 min each: continuous pulsing at PRF 250 Hz, 2 ms pulses, 50 % DC; or burst mode with 300-ms pulse trains every 2 s (PRF 250 Hz, 2 ms pulses, 50 % intra-train DC, total DC 7.5 %). MEPs measured about 5 min before and after.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The study included 50 rats, divided into five groups: control, highduty cycle pulsed ultrasound at low intensity, high-duty cycle pulsed ultrasound at high intensity, low-duty cycle burst-mode pulsed ultrasound at low intensity, high-duty cycle burst-mode pulsed ultrasound at high intensity (n = 10 per group).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: MEP measurements were taken approximately five minutes after the LIFU session. Each experiment lasted between 35 and 40 min.

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: Two stimulation protocols were applied, both delivering the same total acoustic energy but differing in temporal structure. The first protocol employed a high-duty cycle pulsed ultrasound condition with a PRF of 250 Hz, a pulse duration of 2 ms, and a 50 % duty cycle (DC) (Fig. 1e). The second protocol used a low-duty cycle burst-mode pulsed ultrasound, consisting of 300-millisecond pulse trains delivered every 2 s. Within each train, pulses were delivered at a PRF of 250 Hz with a 2-millisecond pulse duration and a 50 % intra-train DC, resulting in a total DC of 7.5 %
